findings.claim: Keyboard selection of a highlighted command has no navigation handler: `Autocomplete.Root` defines no `onValueChange`, and navigation is wired only to item `onClick`, so pressing Enter on the auto-highlighted result may only commit the input value instead of navigating.
findings.evidence: `Autocomplete.Root` props are `open inline items itemToStringValue autoHighlight="always" keepHighlight` with no selection callback; the only `navigateTo` call is `onClick={() => navigateTo(destination)}` on `Autocomplete.Item`. The footer advertises 'Enter' for selection, the spec requires 'SHALL auto-highlight keyboard results ... close after selection', and the only keyboard test (app-shell.test.tsx) clicks the item with the pointer after asserting focus.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `onValueChange={(destination) => navigateTo(destination)}` (or Base UI's documented selection callback) on `Autocomplete.Root`, guard against non-destination values, and add a test that presses Enter on the highlighted item and asserts navigation.

findings.claim: Removing the admin shell's Ctrl/Cmd+K keydown listener regresses the existing cmdk palette's keyboard access and can produce two stacked modal dialogs with competing focus traps.
findings.evidence: The deleted hunk removes the only visible keyboard trigger for `setCommandOpen`, while `commandOpen` state and `setCommandOpen(false)` in `handleSelect` remain (the legacy cmdk dialog is retained per the constraints' 'Keep cmdk installed for existing consumers'). The new global palette binds the same shortcut in app-shell.tsx (`document.addEventListener("keydown", openCommandPalette)`), so on /admin routes Ctrl+K now opens the Base UI palette even while the legacy palette is open, and the legacy palette has no keyboard path at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Either route the admin palette's open state through the new shell palette, or explicitly document/remove the legacy dialog trigger so only one palette is reachable per route.

findings.claim: The breadcrumb section logic mislabels non-Configure destinations: every non-configure group, including the `system` destination About and any unmatched path, renders under 'Workspace'.
findings.evidence: `const section = destination?.group === "configure" ? "Configure" : "Workspace";` — `/about` (group `system` in nav-destinations.ts) renders 'Workspace/About', and an unmatched path falls back to label 'Workspace', producing 'Workspace/Workspace'. The spec requires the breadcrumb to derive accurately from the shared destination inventory.
findings.suggested_fix: Map all three groups explicitly (work → Workspace, configure → Configure, system → System or About-only label) and use a neutral fallback for unmatched paths.

findings.claim: The compact Configure tab identifies the current location only visually; unlike the sibling links it has no `aria-current`, so the current-location signal the spec mandates for the Configure tab is absent for assistive technology.
findings.evidence: The spec scenario states 'the matching Configure item and compact Configure tab MUST identify the current location'. The three `Link` targets set `aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}`, but the Configure `<button>` only toggles classes via `configureActive` and has no `aria-current` (or equivalent pressed/current semantics tied to the active route).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `aria-current={configureActive ? "page" : undefined}` (or an equivalent accessible indication) to the Configure button when a configure route is active.

findings.claim: The newly committed registry references a `markdown-lazy-blocks` artifact directory that is neither added in this diff nor present in the repository tree, leaving a dead registry entry.
findings.evidence: registry.json (new file) maps `"markdown-lazy-blocks": { "path": ".refiner/artifacts/markdown-lazy-blocks" ... }`, but the diff adds only `.refiner/artifacts/app-shell-and-navigation/*` and the file tree contains no `.refiner` directory at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the referenced artifact directory with the registry, or omit the entry until its artifact lands.

findings.claim: Both favicon links are gated behind `prefers-color-scheme` media queries with no unconditional fallback, so browsers that ignore `media` on icon links (notably older Safari) get no favicon at all.
findings.evidence: The removed line was an unconditional `<link rel="icon" ... href="/favicon.svg" />`; the replacement provides only `media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"` and `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"` variants.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one media-less `<link rel="icon" href="/brand/uar-favicon-dark.svg" />` (or .ico) as the default and use the media-scoped links as overrides.

findings.claim: The single PWA icon declares `"purpose": "any maskable"` for a single 512px asset; combining purposes means the same artwork is used in the maskable safe zone, which the square logo-with-rounded-rect artwork likely was not designed for.
findings.evidence: The manifest now contains only one icon entry (`/brand/png/uar-appicon-dark-512.png`) with `purpose: "any maskable"`, replacing the previous plain `any` 180x180 entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide separate `any` and `maskable` icon entries, with padding-safe artwork for the maskable variant.

findings.claim: The design document names the new store field `mobileSheet`, but the implementation, hook, and tests all use `shellSheet`, leaving the binding design artifact out of sync with the shipped code.
findings.evidence: design.md Decision 4: 'The existing UI store gains `navRailCollapsed`, `commandPaletteOpen`, and `mobileSheet`'; ui-store.ts defines `shellSheet: ShellSheet` and `setShellSheet`.
findings.suggested_fix: Update design.md to reference `shellSheet` (or rename the store field) so the acceptance authority matches the implementation.
